html: A rise in cytosolic calcium is read by calmodulin, which binds four calcium ions and then activates the calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinases. CaMKII, made from four genes with different tissue distributions, phosphorylates many targets and joins inflammatory signalling. Calmodulin also activates CaMKK1 and CaMKK2, which phosphorylate and activate CaMKIV, a kinase of the nucleus that regulates transcription. Calcium signals reach the ERK cascade through these kinases.
